question.problem: Let $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{3}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}).$ Given that $C$ is the path along the curve $y=2{x}^{2}$ for $x\in [-1,2],$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a piecewise-smooth curve given by the vector function $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b].$ Let $f$ be a differentiable function of two or three variables such that $∇f$ is continuous on $C.$ The fundamental theorem for line integrals states that 

$$
{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r=f(r(b))-f(r(a)).
$$

We start by parametrizing the curve $C.$ A suitable parametrization is

$$
r(t)=⟨t,2{t}^{2}⟩,\,t\in [-1,2].
$$

Then, the position vectors of the endpoints of the curve are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨-1,2⟩, \\ r(2) & =⟨2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the endpoints of the path defined by $C$ are $(-1,2)$ and $(2,8).$

Applying the fundamental theorem for line integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r & =f(r(2))-f(r(-1)) \\  & =f(2,8)-f(-1,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({2}^{3}+{8}^{3})-\frac{1}{3}((-1)^{3}+{2}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(520)-\frac{1}{3}(7) \\  & =\frac{520}{3}-\frac{7}{3} \\  & =171.\end{aligned}
$$
